validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION: a real trunk gas pipeline named 'Taganrog-Melitopol' (Таганрог-Мелитополь), running from Taganrog (Rostov Oblast, Russia) through occupied Donetsk territory to Melitopol (Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine), is independently attested across 2022-2025 by multiple distinct outlets: Kommersant (2022-07-12, private Russian business daily, sourced to Russian Ministry of Energy insiders — https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/5459063), neftegaz.ru (Russian trade press, two separate 2022 articles citing local officials' own statements — https://neftegaz.ru/news/gazoraspredelenie/744846-.../ and .../756746-.../), DAN/Donetsk News Agency (2023-07-27, quoting DNR deputy PM Andrey Chertkov by name — https://dan-news.ru/ekonomika/nachata-prokladka-magistralnogo-gazoprovoda-taganrog-melitopol/, also mirrored in English at https://dan-news.ru/en/economy/taganrog-melitopol-gas-pipeline-project-underway/), and TASS (2024-04-29, same Chertkov, live URL now 403s but content recovered via Wayback — https://web.archive.org/web/20240507231951/https://tass.ru/obschestvo/20680005). The TASS/Wayback text explicitly calls it a 'магистральный газопровод \"Таганрог-Мелитополь\"' (trunk/transmission gas pipeline) and says it now supplies Zaporizhzhia ('Запорожье') as well as southern DNR -- consistent with Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission as recorded. CAVEAT (per country-scope guidance): every one of these sources is Russian state media, Russian trade press, or a DNR/occupation-administration mouthpiece reporting the SAME official's statements -- per the standing rule this counts as one origin bucket, tier medium at best, for the existence/classification finding even though the count of distinct outlets is >1. I found no Ukrainian-government or Western outlet naming this specific pipeline; the closest independent Ukrainian source I found (ria-m.tv/RIA-Pivden, an exile Melitopol outlet, https://ria-m.tv/news/375505/proshli-berdyansk-rossiya-stroit-nefteprovod-v-kryim-cherez-okkupirovannyiy-melitopol.html, 2025-04-04, citing the Center for Studying Occupation and Mariupol-mayor adviser Petro Andriushchenko) independently confirms Russia is building oil+gas pipeline infrastructure through Berdyansk toward Melitopol/Crimea -- corroborating the CORRIDOR's reality from a genuinely independent angle, but describing a pipeline-construction phase that started July 2024, i.e. a later/different segment than the one this row's refs describe (see spec concern on dates below).

validity.recommendation: Flag for cluster-level adjudication against P1488 ('Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk Gas Pipeline' rebuild, named in the sweep's occupied-territory guidance but outside this row's given roster) -- do not merge/edit unilaterally.
validity.researcher_notes: The historical record shows this corridor is made of at least TWO distinct physical components, and P5989's own compound name ('Taganrog-Melitopol-Berdyansk') plus its wiki slug (just 'Taganrog-Melitopol', no Berdyansk) suggest GEM may be folding them together or mis-splitting them against a sibling row. Per Kommersant (2022-07-12) and neftegaz.ru (2022-10-31, https://neftegaz.ru/news/gazoraspredelenie/756746-v-melitopole-nachali-podavat-gaz/): Russia's plan had TWO parts -- (1) restore the pre-existing, then-INACTIVE ('недействующий') Soviet-era trunk Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk (Gazprom-era asset, per a separately-found neftegaz headline 'Власти ДНР намерены восстановить газопровод Таганрог-Мариуполь, принадлежащий Газпрому'), and (2) build a genuinely NEW pipeline section Berdyansk-Melitopol ('от Бердянска до Мелитополя нужно было строить новый [участок]'), reported >100 km by Kommersant. Gas reached Berdyansk 2022-10-25 and Melitopol 2022-10-31 per neftegaz, citing then-acting Zaporizhzhia governor Balitsky. The scope guidance for this sweep explicitly names 'the Russian-built Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk rebuild' as touching P1488 (not included in the 9-row roster I was given for direct comparison). If P1488 already records the restored old Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk segment, P5989 -- whose own name spans Taganrog...Berdyansk AND Melitopol -- risks double-counting that same restored trunk under a second, broader-named row. I have not resolved this (per the sweep's own rule not to adjudicate clusters solo); it needs a side-by-side compare of P5989 vs P1488 on endpoints/length/ConstructionYear.

validity.recommendation: Re-verify StartYear1: independent 2022 reporting places actual gas delivery into Melitopol at 2022-10-31, roughly 1.5 years before the recorded StartYear1=2024. Also re-examine ConstructionYear=2023/07: the sheet's own cited source (dan-news, verified live) describes a mid-life RE-LAY/upgrade of an existing, previously leaky pipe ('перекладка'), not the pipeline's original construction -- confirmed independently by the TASS/Wayback follow-up article, which quotes the same DNR official saying 'старые трубы были попросту дырявыми' (the old pipes were simply full of holes) before the 2023 work. Do not silently keep 2023/2024 as founding dates without settling whether they describe the ORIGINAL build (per neftegaz, ~2022) or a documented later capacity upgrade.
validity.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2024, sourced to the now-dead TASS link: the TASS article recovered via Wayback (dated 2024-04-29) reports the EFFECTS of a 2023 upgrade being felt in winter 2023-24 (doubled pipeline pressure, 1.5x more gas volume, no more heating-season rationing) -- it does not claim the pipeline started operating in 2024. Independent, earlier reporting (neftegaz.ru, 2022-10-31, citing acting Zaporizhzhia governor Balitsky) states gas was already flowing into Melitopol on 2022-10-31, after Berdyansk received it on 2022-10-25 -- i.e. the pipeline (or at least the new Berdyansk-Melitopol section that reaches Melitopol) was delivering gas nearly a year and a half before the sheet's recorded StartYear1. ConstructionYear=2023/Month=7, sourced to dan-news (verified live, dated exactly 2023-07-27, matching the value): the DNR official's own quoted words are 'начаты работы по ПЕРЕКЛАДКЕ магистрального газопровода Таганрог-Мелитополь' -- 'relaying/re-laying', i.e. replacing pipe on an EXISTING corridor, not new construction from scratch. The TASS/Wayback follow-up (2024-04-29) confirms this was pipe replacement on old, deteriorated infrastructure ('старые трубы были попросту дырявыми'). Taken together, the two cited events (dan-news 2023-07, TASS 2024-04) appear to document a 2023 REHABILITATION/upgrade of an already-operating corridor, not the corridor's origin -- the corridor's actual first gas delivery to Melitopol traces independently to 2022-10-31 (neftegaz.ru).

fills.researcher_notes: TASS/Wayback names the pipeline 'Таганрог-Мелитополь' explicitly and states it supplies Zaporizhzhia ('Запорожье'), matching EndState/Province=Zaporizhzhia Oblast and EndLocation=Melitopol. DAN independently confirms the same pipeline name and that it passes through DNR territory en route (consistent with a Taganrog, Russia origin). Taganrog itself being in Rostov Oblast is undisputed public geography, not separately sourced. Tier medium and independent=false per the country-scope rule: both citing sources are Russian state/occupation-linked outlets reporting the same DNR official's statements, i.e. one origin bucket, not two independent ones -- flagging explicitly rather than claiming high confidence.

summary: P5989 (Taganrog-Melitopol-Berdyansk) is a real, correctly classified Russian-built gas trunk into occupied Zaporizhzhia -- but existence support is single-origin-bucket (Russian/DNR state media only, tier medium); StartYear1=2024 looks too late (independent 2022 reporting has gas reaching Melitopol 2022-10-31) and ConstructionYear=2023/07 documents a re-lay/upgrade of already-existing pipe, not original construction; flagged as a likely DUPLICATE/overlap with P1488's Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk rebuild for cluster adjudication; filled the missing Location [ref] at tier medium.
